changes: Era set to VS: the colophon gives the year as 'saṃvaṃt 1750'. 'śake' has no number after it, so it is an unfilled or broken Śaka slot, not a second year. ce_approx = 1694. This conflicts with the catalogue's ŚS 1750 (c. 1828), which is recorded in notes.
Removed residence 'Revāgrāma' from p1. The colophon names Revāgrāma only as the place of copying, not where the scribe lives.
Moved 'chandoga' (Sāmavedin school designation) from titles to affiliation; 'dīkṣita' stays in titles.
Weekday normalised to 'budhavāsara (Wednesday)'; paksa given as 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)'.
Changed purpose to read 'for himself and for others'. Both phrases are kept in purpose.

date.as_written: saṃvaṃt 1750 samaye phālguṇa śake (1) vadi 8 aṣṭamī budhavāsare

purpose: svārthaṃ paramārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: Era conflict: the colophon gives the year 1750 explicitly as 'saṃvaṃt', which in a North Indian Devanagari colophon normally means Vikrama → c. 1694 CE (Phālguna VS 1750 ≈ Feb/Mar 1694). The word 'śake' follows the month with no number before the line break. It looks like an unfilled or broken Śaka slot (Phālguna śake might be meant as 'Phālguna in the Śaka year', i.e. Śaka 1615). The catalogue's 'ŚS 1750' (c. 1828 CE) looks like it applies the Śaka label to the saṃvat number. I have not checked the weekday (Wednesday, kṛṣṇa 8) against either year. Doing so would settle VS 1750 vs ŚS 1750. 'Chandoga' marks the scribe as a Sāmavedin. Revāgrāma is not identified (possibly a village on the Revā/Narmadā). The final verse 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā...' is a standard scribal formula. 'bhavānī' is an invocation, not a person.
